newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM TO BRIEF CABINET ON NATIVE TITLE
The Federal Government's deliberations in response to the High Court's Wik ruling move into a new phase tomorrow, with the Prime Minister expected to brief Cabinet.
A Government source says Mr Howard feels it's time to move to a point when a clear decision needs to be made.

A spokesperson says the Government's working hard to seek agreement between all parties on a package that provides certainty to pastoralists and miners and respects the interests of indigenous Australians.
WOOLDRIDGE ANNOUNCES RURAL HEALTH INITIATIVE

The Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, says the shortage of doctors in regional Australia has reached crisis point, and has announced a new initiative to get medical students to work in rural areas.
Dr Wooldridge awarded the first of the 150 John Flyn scholarships to three of Monash University's top medical students, in Melbourne.
The students will be posted to rural and Aboriginal communities throughout Australia, and Dr Wooldridge says the scholarships are designed to improve health services in the bush.
WOOLWORTH'S TRADE RESULTS "PLEASING"
Retail group, Woolworth's has described its latest sales results as pleasing, in difficult trading conditions.
The group has posted sales for the past 40 weeks of just under 11.8 billion dollars, up one billion dollars on the same period the previous year.
Sales in the past 12 weeks have also improved on the corresponding period last year.
The company says there was strong growth in both food and general merchandise, but women's clothing continues to be a problem.
NEW PETROLEUM PERMITS
The Australian Government has called for applicants for 34 new petroluem exploration permits, one of which covers Australia's most populated coastline.
Seven of the new permits cover waters adjacent to the Timor Gap Zone of Co-operation in Australia's northern waters.

The permit covering the Sydney basin, the country's most heavily populated coastline, begins six-kilometres offshore and stretches from Port Stephens, north of Sydney, to Stanwell Park to the city's south.
A spokesman for Energy and Resources Minister, Warwick Parer, says he expects controversy over the Sydney basin permit given its size and proximity to the coast.
GUN CONTROL COALITION REJECTS CLAIMS BUY BACK ISN'T WORKING
The National Coalition for Gun Control says figures from the gun buy-back scheme are showing that Australia is on the way to becoming a safer place.
Australians have handed in more than 372-thousand prohibited weapons under the national buyback scheme.
Compensation totalling more than 186-million dollars has been paid.

Rebecca Peters from the National Coalition for Gun Control, says claims by the gun lobby the scheme isn't working are wrong. She says figures from Victoria show that only one in ten guns handed back have been replaced with another gun.
SHORT LIST FOR CASA BOARD NEW APPOINTEES
Federal Transport Minister John Sharp is finalising his short list for new appointees to the Board of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority.
Mr Sharp has considered more than 100 possible nominees for the new positions, and a spokesman says the short-list will be taken to Cabinet in the not too distant future.
Mr Sharp's office is not commenting on whether businessman and aviator Dick Smith is one of those under consideration, although industry sources expect him to be on the Minister's short-list.
Mr Sharp has said previously that Mr Smith would be on anybody's short-list given his aviation experience and desire to implement change.
The appointment of the new Board members will increase Mr Sharp's influence over the Board, after spending the last year calling for the existing directors' resignations.
14 TREATED AFTER ANOTHER FOOD POISONING OUTBREAK
Fourteen people have been treated at Melbourne hospitals following another outbreak of food poisoning over the weekend.

All of the people suffered acute gastro enteritis after attending an Indonesian Food Festival at the Malvern Town Hall. The Department of Human Services says anyone who consumed food at the festival, and is experiencing stomach pains, vomiting or diarrhoea, should seek prompt medical treatment.
PAULINE HANSON "HAS A DREAM"
Independent Federal MP Pauline Hanson says she can relate to the famous "I have a dream" speech by American civil rights leader, Martin Luther King.
Ms Hanson says while it will be hard to keep her finger on the pulse all the time, she's pledged to ensure racists aren't involved with her newly launched "One Nation" party.

Appearing on the Nine Network's Midday program, Ms Hanson said she identified with Martin Luther King' speech, in which he looked to the day when his children would not be judged by the colour of their skin, but the content of their character.
She said she deplores intolerance, and believes she is also saying that people should not be judged by the colour of their skin.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
